hero.subline: for Generation Z & Alpha — knowledgeable and safe in the digital environment
hero.body: Z & Alpha Initiative is a pioneering project in Vietnam, dedicated to enhancing digital awareness, digital skills, and mental well-being for young people in the technology era. We believe that a healthy digital world can only be built when the younger generations are equipped with deep knowledge, empathy, and enduring human values.

featured.fallbackDesc: 72 Hours Without Facebook introduces a small-scale experiment exploring how young people respond, adapt, and self-regulate when temporarily stepping away from a familiar social media platform.

what.lead: Z & Alpha Initiative operates at the intersection of research, education, and policy, aiming to build a healthy digital environment for the next generations.
what.bullet1: Conducting in-depth studies on the social, psychological, and behavioral impacts of the digital environment on adolescents.
what.bullet2: Providing policy recommendations and evidence-based insights for schools, parents, and regulatory bodies.
what.bullet3: Organizing training programs, workshops, and communication campaigns to raise community awareness about safe and healthy social media use.
what.principleText: Across all our work, intellectual independence is a core value.
what.principleCta: Read about our funding & independence policy

card1.title: Education
card1.body: Designing curricula, workshops, and guidelines to help students, teachers, and parents better understand digital literacy, critical thinking skills, and mental health in the age of social media.

card2.title: Policy Recommendations
card2.body: Providing data and empirical evidence to agencies and organizations in developing policies related to children and young people in the digital environment.

card3.title: Research
card3.body: Conducting qualitative, quantitative, and interdisciplinary research on the relationship between technology, psychology, and society, particularly focusing on the 13–18 age group.

aboutSocialMedia.metaTitle: Social media and Vietnam's next generation — Z & Alpha
aboutSocialMedia.heroSubtitle: Sự tái cấu trúc toàn diện tuổi thơ trong kỷ nguyên số
aboutSocialMedia.heroLead: Why Z & Alpha exists — and the scientific context we draw on to understand Vietnam's young generation.

scholar.name: Jonathan Haidt
scholar.role: Professor of Social Psychology, NYU Stern
scholar.phd: PhD in Social Psychology, University of Pennsylvania
scholar.expertise: Research on moral foundations, social behavior, and the impact of technology on young generations
scholar.published: 2024, synthesizing data from large-scale surveys (tens of thousands of respondents, 2010–2023)
scholar.scope: U.S., Canada, Australia, and European countries

aboutSocialMedia.quote: Children are shifting from a development environment grounded in real-world experience to one mediated entirely through screens.
aboutSocialMedia.vnContextBody: Vietnam is among the countries where the "rewiring of childhood" is unfolding at an exceptionally fast pace. Social media adoption among youth is near-universal and reliance on mobile devices is unusually high.
aboutSocialMedia.featuresHeading: Defining traits of the digital environment Vietnam's young generation is growing up in

features.label: Always-On Connectivity
features.body: Platforms engineer continuous notifications and real-time update loops, keeping users in an almost uninterrupted online state.

features.label: Digital-First Social Interaction
features.labelEn: Tương tác xã hội qua nền tảng số
features.body: Most communication — messaging, sharing, making friends, entertainment — now happens inside social apps, gradually replacing in-person interaction.

features.label: Blurred Digital-Physical Boundaries
features.labelEn: Ranh giới thực – ảo ngày càng mờ
features.body: Personalised content and the habit of broadcasting daily life means online experience both reflects and reshapes offline behaviour. Learning, leisure, shopping, and self-presentation all play out across both spaces in parallel.

aboutSocialMedia.impactHeading: How social media is impacting Vietnam's young generation
aboutSocialMedia.impactLead: Vietnam is on the trajectory Haidt describes, but with greater intensity given its "mobile-first society" characteristics. The impact is not just about content — it's an ecosystem shaping behaviour, psychology, and the social development of children.

direct.title: Attention fragmentation
direct.body: Restructuring of behaviour and attention capacity (attention fragmentation)

direct.title: Anxiety & social comparison
direct.body: Psychological impact: anxiety, social comparison, and self-evaluation

indirect.title: Infrastructure of risk
indirect.body: Scams targeting children are rarely separable from social media

indirect.title: Psychological manipulation in scams
indirect.body: Mechanisms exploiting psychology through digital platforms
